summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause: there are no confirmed US or Israeli strikes on Iran in recent weeks, but Iran is still attacking ships around the Strait of Hormuz, the US blockade of Iranian ports continues, and talks on a new draft deal are under way. Hormuz is open only in part, with oil flows well below normal.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are open under US control. Most ships now pass through a US-run transit system (101 transits over Oct 22–24, against about 138 a day in 2025), with only a handful a day outside it.

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: Around 11.6 to 11.7 million barrels a day in October, against about 17.1 million before the war (Kpler).

status.label: The war
status.note: No confirmed US or Israeli strikes on Iran in recent weeks (AFP reported none on Iranian targets since early September). Trump said on Oct 8 the US would not resume strikes before the Nov 3 midterms; reports say renewed strikes are being prepared for after that.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent near US$113.7 and WTI near US$100.8 at about 12:25 p.m. ET on Oct 29 (Trading Economics), down about 1.4% and 1.9% on the day; the year high is near US$126.

updates.text: AP reported that Lloyd's List Intelligence says tankers are still moving oil through the strait under US military protection despite the recent attacks; AP could not confirm Iran's claim that three tankers hit mines, and UKMTO reported one burning vessel without details of crew or damage.
sources: AP via ClickOrlando, Oct 29: Iran says 3 oil tankers struck mines, and other Mideast news

updates.text: Iran's Fars news agency carried a Revolutionary Guard statement saying three tankers had struck sea mines in the southern passage of the Strait of Hormuz and were on fire; the claim was not independently verified, and it was unclear whether it referred to the ship UKMTO reported on fire off Khasab.
sources: AP via Yahoo News, Oct 29: Ship on fire in Strait of Hormuz, UK agency says

updates.text: UKMTO said it received a report from the master of a passing ship of a vessel on fire about 9 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz; the cause and the crew's status were not known.
sources: Arab News, Oct 29: Ship on fire in Strait of Hormuz, says maritime agency

updates.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it shot down a US MQ-1 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz, off Sirik in Hormozgan province, calling it the 14th MQ-1 it has downed; no US response was reported.
sources: Trend.Az, Oct 29: IRGC says U.S. MQ-1 drone shot down east of Strait of Hormuz
Siasat, Oct 29: Didn't start war, says Trump as IRGC claims US-made drone downed

updates.text: Trump denied reports that he had directed Vice President JD Vance to begin peace talks with Iran, saying the contact concerned Tehran's need for help with medical supplies.
sources: Al Jazeera Iran war live, Oct 29

updates.text: Araghchi said Tehran remains in close and ongoing contact with mediators on implementing a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
sources: Al Jazeera Iran war live, Oct 29

updates.text: US Central Command said reports in Iranian-controlled media of commercial ships striking sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz were false, and that the primary transit routes cleared by US forces remain clear.
sources: Gulf News, Oct 29: US military rejects Iranian mine-strike claims

updates.text: Bloomberg reported that the US told ships to avoid unnecessary transits through the Strait of Hormuz.
sources: Bloomberg, Oct 28: US tells ships to avoid unnecessary transits through Hormuz

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
